title: Optional properties (?), undefined, and exactOptionalPropertyTypes
hook: The question mark on a property means the key may be absent or undefined — but exactOptionalPropertyTypes draws a finer line between missing and explicitly undefined. C# string? is similar at compile time; neither stops bad JSON at runtime.

blocks.text: **Optional properties** use `prop?: T` syntax, equivalent to `prop: T | undefined` for read purposes. The key may be **missing** from the object or present with value `undefined`. **`exactOptionalPropertyTypes`** (separate from strict) distinguishes: with it on, you cannot assign `undefined` to an optional property unless the type explicitly includes `undefined`. **`strictNullChecks`** must be on for optional semantics to matter. At runtime JavaScript simply omits keys or sets them to undefined — no compile-time distinction survives emit.

entries.plainDefinition: Property that may be absent; typed as T | undefined when read.
Flag: optional means missing only, not explicitly undefined, unless union includes undefined.
Utility making all properties optional — common for PATCH DTOs.

blocks.text: REST PATCH endpoints often send partial objects — optional properties model that. Confusing `?` with nullable `| null` causes API bugs: `email?: string` allows missing but not necessarily null unless you add `| null`. Redis and JSON may omit keys or send null — validate at boundaries. C# `string?` on a property is compile-time nullable; TypeScript optional is about key presence.

blocks.title: Three-way distinction
blocks.body: Required: must be present. Optional (?): may be absent. Nullable (| null): may be null when present. Combine: email?: string | null for all cases.

items.title: Optional for PATCH
items.body: Partial<T> or explicit optional fields for update DTOs.

items.title: exactOptionalPropertyTypes
items.body: Enable when you need missing vs undefined distinction in APIs.

snippet.label: exactOptionalPropertyTypes difference
snippet.explanation: Without the flag, undefined assignment is allowed. With it, optional means key absent only — stricter API contracts.

blocks.title: Treating ? as null-safe
blocks.body: Optional means undefined/missing — not null. API null requires | null in the type.

blocks.text: exactOptionalPropertyTypes interacts with spread: { ...obj, key: undefined } may delete vs set undefined depending on target. Required<T> and Partial<T> are duals for CRUD DTO layers. For OpenAPI codegen, optional fields map to ? — verify null vs absent in schema. Senior teams document three states: required, optional-absent, nullable-present.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected
blocks.body: Saying ? means nullable. Not knowing exactOptionalPropertyTypes exists. Using ! on optional fields instead of narrowing.

interviewTakeaways: prop?: T means key may be absent; type is T | undefined when read.
? is not the same as | null — model JSON null explicitly.
60s: Optional for absent keys. Narrow before use. Partial for PATCH. C# string? parallels nullable; TS ? parallels optional key. Runtime: validate API shape.
Follow-up: Partial vs Pick for update DTOs?
commonPitfalls: Weak: email?: string allows null from API — it does not unless | null added.
Weak: accessing optional without check — use ?. or if !== undefined.
Strong: Three states: required, optional absent, nullable. exactOptionalPropertyTypes for strict APIs. Partial for patches.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS returns undefined for missing keys — optional ? documents that behavior at compile time.
Partial<T> maps all properties to optional — built on the same optional property semantics.
